clue.text: A Latin ladies' man found everywhere

parts.note: a ladies' man is a womaniser, a lover

explanation.surface: A Roman Casanova turns up wherever you look.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread across every place is all over it, an idiom for ubiquitous.

clue.text: Historical records about university published each year

indicators.note: the records word sits around the university letter, enclosing it

parts.note: annals are year-by-year historical records

explanation.surface: University chronicles issued every twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the answer is: annuals are books or plants renewed each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are yearbooks issued once a year, things that come out yearly.

clue.text: The blooming result of slothful passion

definitions.text: The blooming result of slothful passion

parts.words: The blooming result of slothful passion
parts.note: a flower name read literally as romance found in laziness; blooming means it is a plant

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark about what lazy lust produces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' looks like a mild British swear-word, but it means flowering: the answer is an old name for the wild pansy.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-idleness is the folk name for the wild pansy, and literally passion when idle.

clue.text: Actual part of River Yar

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A real stretch of the Yar, a river on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Very as an adjective means actual or precise, as in the very thing.

clue.text: Lie about Conservative party policy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the party line is its official policy

explanation.surface: A politician's dishonesty regarding Tory policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' suggests a falsehood, but it means lie down.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lie back at rest.

clue.text: Rose has to clip the edges

definitions.meaning: a garden flower and also a rosy colour
to ... cloth is to cut its edge in a zigzag, as ... shears do

explanation.surface: A rose bush needs its borders trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose as a pale red colour, and the dressmaker's verb for cutting a serrated edge to stop fraying.

clue.text: Poser for the French in British Museum

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: the French article goes inside the museum abbreviation

parts.note: BM is the British Museum in London
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A model posing for French visitors at the British Museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poser' suggests someone striking a pose, but it means a puzzling question.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a difficult question, a puzzle to solve.

clue.text: Food served without appeal for quiet

parts.note: no means lacking, without
sh is the plea for silence

explanation.surface: A meal dished up with no request for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for grub.

clue.text: Leave wife to pay half

parts.note: to go is to leave
Dutch is Cockney slang for wife, from duchess, as in my old Dutch

explanation.surface: Advice to abandon your spouse so you only pay half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is old London Cockney slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is to split the bill evenly, each paying a share.

clue.text: Had it explained why Liz Taylor left husband number four

definitions.meaning: to be ruined or dead, British slang from the RAF

definitions.text: explained why Liz Taylor left husband number four
definitions.meaning: Elizabeth Taylor left her fourth husband Eddie Fisher for the actor Richard Burton

explanation.surface: Gossip about why a film star walked out on a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means wrecked or killed; read literally, Taylor went off to Richard Burton.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for being ruined or lost, and literally Taylor departing for the actor Burton.

clue.text: Perfect peace after the puzzle has been dropped

definitions.text: Perfect peace after the puzzle has been dropped

parts.words: Perfect peace after the puzzle has been dropped
parts.note: read one way, a household where nobody ever speaks angrily; read another, a home that has stopped buying the newspaper puzzle

explanation.surface: Domestic calm returns once the daily brain-teaser is abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes total harmony with no angry words, while the puzzle reading says that word-grid is gone for good.

clue.text: Keen to see commercial about the Virgin Islands

indicators.note: the advert word goes around the islands abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an AD
VI is the abbreviation for the Virgin Islands

explanation.surface: Someone eager to watch a holiday advert for the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and avid are synonyms for enthusiastic.

clue.text: Can get by without misfortune

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word by surrounds the other piece

parts.note: ill as a noun means harm or misfortune

explanation.surface: Advice that you can manage to avoid bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is a noun: a billycan is a camping cooking pot. 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy is the tin pot campers boil water in, also called a billycan.

clue.text: Propensity to be dishonest

definitions.meaning: slang for corrupt, as a crooked police officer

explanation.surface: A natural tendency towards crookedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning inclination, and a British slang adjective meaning corrupt.

clue.text: Dandies upset about old trick

indicators.note: the turned dandies word sits around the old letter
in a down clue upset turns the dandies word upside down, reading it bottom to top

parts.note: fops are vain dandies

explanation.surface: Flashy dressers annoyed by an ancient con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FOPS into SPOF, which goes 'about' O.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a hoax or prank.

clue.text: Loud kiss is suggestive

definitions.meaning: to ... of something is to hint at it

explanation.surface: A noisy smooch carries a hint of something more.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy peck, and the verb that, followed by of, means hints at.

clue.text: A small drink may roughen one's exterior

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A nip of spirits might coarsen your complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling a wall or painted surface dabs it into a textured, dotted finish.

clue.text: Mother pursued by lepidopterous insect of huge size

indicators.note: the mother word comes first with the insect chasing behind it

parts.note: MAM is an informal, chiefly northern British word for mother
a moth belongs to the order Lepidoptera along with butterflies

explanation.surface: A mother being chased by a monstrous butterfly-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the name of the extinct woolly elephant means gigantic.

clue.text: Shout for the linesman to declare the ball long

definitions.text: for the linesman to declare the ball long
definitions.meaning: in tennis the line judge calls a ball out when it lands beyond the baseline

explanation.surface: A tennis official yelling that a shot went past the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for yelling, and the tennis official's ruling that a ball landed past the line.

clue.text: Many damaged when put under a spell

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
harmed means damaged or hurt

explanation.surface: Lots of people got hurt once bewitched.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed means enchanted, under magic.

clue.text: Mulled claret a year after becomes very sweet

indicators.note: the year letter is placed after the rearranged wine
mulled wine is spiced and stirred, so the word claret is rearranged

explanation.surface: Spiced red wine, a year on, becomes sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacly means as sweet as treacle, a British name for molasses.

clue.text: Current demand for public approval

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a claim is a demand for something as one's due

explanation.surface: Electricity suppliers seeking popular support.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic praise from the public.

clue.text: Aimed to construct a church feature with copper base

parts.note: a spire is a church's pointed steeple
a copper was a penny coin, D in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Building a church steeple on a copper foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' puts the D at the bottom of this down answer; 'copper' is the metal in surface but a penny coin, D, in old British money.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's sights on a goal.

clue.text: Hindu psalm chanted softly can hold one ensnared

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred Hindu chant
p is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Hindu chanting softly can captivate a listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer, a trap for catching people.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a device for catching trespassers, holding them captive.

clue.text: Spots one around noon

indicators.note: the word for one wraps itself around the letter for noon

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A teenager noticing a pimple at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is the skin condition of pimples, so spots as a noun.

clue.text: Jumped in the field to take exercise

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone bounding across a meadow during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is a past tense of leap, a synonym of jump.

clue.text: British vessel set on fire

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A British ship is torched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container, an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn something is to ignite it.

clue.text: Apprehension felt by Egyptian in remote surroundings

indicators.note: the remote word forms surroundings around the Egyptian letter

parts.note: far means remote, distant
E is the abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: An Egyptian feeling anxious in a distant land.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension means dread or anxiety.

clue.text: Cardinal meets artist-a divine female

parts.note: HE is His Eminence, a cardinal's title
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A churchman meets a painter, a godlike woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods, a goddess.

clue.text: Turner designed recent, rare stamp

indicators.note: designed signals that these letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: The painter Turner drew a scarce new postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J M W Turner, but it is a woodturner, a skilled craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A master carpenter is a top woodworker, and a turner shapes wood on a lathe.

clue.text: Priest perpetually causing conflict

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is forever stirring up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or fight.

clue.text: Composed when in battle formation

definitions.meaning: ... as a document is drafted or written out
troops ... are arranged in ranks ready to fight

explanation.surface: Battle plans written while soldiers are lined up.
explanation.definitionFit: A drafted document, and soldiers ranged in order for combat.
